title: Choose the round page's visual world
question: The roll assigned Transit Standards. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Dark is the default in every card, as you asked.

options.label: Transit Standards
options.lineage: Vignelli & Noorda's 1970 NYC Transit Authority Graphics Standards Manual
options.thesis: A round page is a wayfinding system: each question is a sign band, and its numbered bullet fills with colour once it's answered.
materials: white grotesk on black sign bands
options.viewport: In the narrow pane: a black header band with the round number and an answered-count, then question bands stacked full-width. Each band opens with a large numbered bullet, the title set in heavy grotesk, and the recommendation as its own row with one Accept key.
options.risk: Bullets in several colours can read as decoration unless every colour means exactly one answer mode.

raised.raise: No card boxes: questions separate by black bands and space alone, and the current question is ranked by brightness, not by a border.
Whole-unit grid: every module is sized in whole 8px units, and the wide tab adds columns in whole units rather than stretching.
Colour lives only in the bullets and one hairline edge. Question text stays achromatic.
Fixed-place counts: '3 of 5 answered' in tabular figures that never reflow.
Past rounds keep every mark. A read-only round shows its answers in place, not as a summary.

options.label: Code Review
options.lineage: pull-request review screens (inline comments, batched 'Submit review')
options.thesis: Answering a round is reviewing a change: comment inline, pick a verdict per item, submit the review once.
options.viewport: Questions as file-like panels, each with a header row; illustrations sit like diffs; a sticky 'Submit round' bar with a pending-comments count.
options.risk: Very familiar, close enough to GitHub that it reads as a clone, and most runs in this category land here.

options.label: Developer Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels divided by one-pixel seams, with syntax colours kept for state only.
options.viewport: The round is a persistent panel stack: questions on the left, the illustration panel expanding along one axis, the design tree as a collapsible panel.
options.case: Wins on audience recognition (it's their editor) but loses on clarity: panels compete with the illustration for attention.
options.risk: Could pass for any dev tool. Nothing says 'decision'.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Questions built cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Huge grid-built question numbers over a visible grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: the visible grid is noise on a task surface.
options.kept: Every module sized in whole units.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.thesis: Bitmap lines riding over a drifting starfield, where rank is depth.
options.viewport: One still bright line per question over drifting layers.
options.case: Loses both axes: drifting motion and a bitmap face fight long reading.
options.kept: No enclosure: rank by brightness, not boxes.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: Achromatic field with colour only at a hairline edge.
options.viewport: White field, spectral hairline marking the active question.
options.case: Loses both axes and fights the dark-mode default.
options.kept: Colour confined to one edge, text stays achromatic.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.viewport: Round progress as a tube bank.
options.case: Loses both axes: a round isn't a quantity.

options.label: Folding Sequence
options.thesis: One sheet carrying every earlier crease.
options.viewport: Numbered folds in a margin column.
options.case: Loses both axes: vermilion ground breaks the dark default and the metaphor is foreign.
options.kept: History stays visible: past rounds keep their marks.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark form stack: rounded question cards, one accent colour, a sticky submit bar, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Centred column of question cards with radio-style answer choices and a sticky 'Submit round' footer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any dark questionnaire, by design.
